title: Configurable PII redaction, retention, and audit events for embeddings & rerank endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Embeddings and reranking workloads currently surface raw request text and derived artifacts in internal logs and observability paths. This increases risk for PII exposure and makes customers hesitant to send sensitive data to hosted endpoints. We need a production-safe controls surface that allows orgs to configure PII handling, retention, and auditable access for embeddings/rerank pipelines without regressing latency or throughput for high-volume workloads.

Scope: Implement endpoint-level and org-level controls for (1) PII detection+redaction prior to any persistent logs, (2) configurable retention TTL for stored embeddings and reranking traces, and (3) an immutable audit event stream for any data access/export of embedding/rerank artifacts. This ticket covers server-side runtime and storage changes, Console UI knobs, and telemetry/audit schema. Does NOT include SDK client-side encryption (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Org admins can set per-org embedding/rerank retention in Console (options: 0/7/30/90/365 days)
PII redaction policy exists and defaults to 'metadata-only' for existing orgs; new orgs default to 'redact-text'
All persisted embedding vectors and rerank traces are tagged with redaction mode and retention TTL in metadata
Audit events are emitted for: data export, retention policy change, manual data deletion, and admin access to raw preserved artifacts
Runtime path avoids >5ms median increase on text->embed/rerank endpoints when redaction is enabled (measured in canary)
E2E tests validate PII patterns are redacted or hashed per policy and that retention purge jobs remove artifacts according to TTL
Security review signoff present and keys used for HMAC hashing are recorded in KMS audit
dependencies: ENG-9180 (Storage TTL index for vector store)
SEC-120 (KMS integration for per-org HMAC keys)
comments: 2025-02-12 — Aisha Patel: Created ticket after customer security review session (large financial customer requested org-level retention and PII redaction for embeddings).

2025-02-18 — Marco Nguyen: Drafted technical design; decided to HMAC-sensitive spans rather than full-text removal for traceability in some audit flows. Performance concerns noted — propose async persistence for full-text logs with sync redaction in hot path.
2025-02-21 — Design review: Sofia Rivera: UX for Console retention selector reviewed. Recommended wording changes for admin impact warnings and an explicit 'Destroy now' button for immediate purge.

2025-02-25 — Security: Priya Shah: Requested threat model and KMS key lifecycle matrix; flagged requirement that HMAC salts be rotated without losing ability to audit (solution: store HMAC key version metadata and rotate by re-hashing new artifacts only).

2025-02-28 — Marco Nguyen: Implemented POC redaction service (golang) that uses a deterministic HMAC for token-level PII and a lightweight regex + heuristic pipeline for emails/SSNs/dates. Benchmarks show p50 overhead ~1.9ms under small text loads; p99 increase observed for long documents — will add size-based fast-path to skip expensive heuristics for >10k chars.

2025-03-03 — Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include explicit audit event types and release target. Prepared migration plan for existing stored embeddings older than 90 days (prior default) to be purged unless org overrides).
